PSAT/SAT Test Administration
• Since 2017 the Rhode Island Department of Education has
 administered the PSAT as part of the spring test administration
 to 10th graders
• Since 2018 the Rhode Island Department of Education has
 administered the SAT to 11th graders.
• Both the PSAT and SAT include sections in ELA and
 Mathematics.

 3

Transition to Digital SAT
• In 2024, the College Board transitioned to the Digital SAT
 administration platform.
• Several aspects of the assessment changed during this transition in
 terms of both user-facing features (computer versus P&P
 administration) as well as backend features (adaptive versus fixed-
 form).
• Changes in the results in 2024 from 2023 led to concern amongst
 some states about test equivalence.
• The analyses in this presentation are intended to support discussions
 about the equivalence of tests and comparability of results.

Introduction
• We examine student performance on the PSAT/SAT in several ways
 • Participation frequencies
 • Mean/Standard Deviations of Scores by year
 • Mean/Median Baseline SGP by year (SAT only)
 • Baseline SGPs are normed using pre-pandemic, PSAT-SAT
 growth norms.

 6

Frequencies
• In general, there was a substantial decrease in participation due to the
 pandemic.
• For the PSAT, the number of students tested has roughly returned to
 pre-pandemic level.
• For the SAT, in 2024 there was a substantial (approximate 8%) increase
 in the number of students tested.

 8

Summary Measures
• Both ELA and Mathematics PSAT saw decreases in mean scaled scores
 over the last six years. The drop in mathematics in 2023-2024 from
 436.4 to 418.4 was particularly large.
• Both ELA and Mathematics PSAT saw increases in the standard
 deviation in 2023-2024 from prior years.
• Both ELA and Mathematics SAT saw decreases in mean scaled scores,
 particularly in 2023-2024. Mathematics dropped from 461.5 to 445.9.
• Both ELA and Mathematics SAT saw increases in standard deviation in
 2023-2024.
• The number of LOSS (200) scores in the SAT saw a large increase in
 2023-2024.

 14

Baseline SGPs
• Because growth is conditioned on prior scores, baseline SGPs are
 much more robust to changes in the population of students tested
 than status measures.
• Baseline SGPs were fairly stable across the last several years in ELA,
 less so in mathematics. The drop in the mean SGP to 44.4 in
 2023-2024 in mathematics is synonymous with the drop in
 achievement observed.
• The low median SGP in mathematics was caused (largely) by low SGPs
 of students in the 6th, 7th, and 8th prior score deciles.
